text: Wynne Neilly, born in 1990, is a Canadian artist and photographer based in Toronto who specializes in photographing queer and transgender individuals. He completed the Image Arts program at Ryerson University, graduating in 2012. Neilly began creating portraiture in the early 2010s and is currently based in Toronto. He identifies as queer and transmasculine, and in 2018, he stated that his maleness is "really only based on my physical appearance," emphasizing that "there is a lot more to me and my gender identity." His artistic focus is on exploring gender and sexuality, particularly "the queer and trans body." In 2014, at the age of 24, a photograph he took was featured on the cover of Original Plumbing, part of a series titled Female to "Male" that centers on gender transitioning and Neilly's own transition. In 2015, he won the "Flash Forward" photography competition hosted by the Magenta Foundation. In 2021, Elliot Page requested that Neilly photograph him for the cover of Time following Page's transition, seeking a transgender photographer. Neilly initially doubted the email, believing the pandemic had ended his career, but he photographed Page on March 5, 2021, for the March 29 – April 5 issue, making him the first transgender man to appear on the magazine's cover. He later expressed that the experience "really meant the world to me to be able to help [Page] tell his story." Neilly draws inspiration from Catherine Opie, as well as Cassils, Michelle Groskopf, and Robert Mapplethorpe. His work has been exhibited at the International Center of Photography, The Annenberg Space for Photography, Southern Norway Art Museum, and the Ryerson Image Centre.
